name: SafeMoon public burn() after upgrade
summary: An upgrade pushed hours before the incident made burn(address,uint256) callable by anyone, so the attacker burned nearly all SFM held by the SafeMoon/WBNB PancakeSwap pair, sync()'d the pool to the inflated SFM price and sold its own SFM back into the drained reserve.
notes: The last of 23 pre-incident Upgraded events selected the implementation that exposed the unrestricted burn(address,uint256) function.

The $8.9 million value is the widely reported gross loss. The structured asset is the exact decrease in the victim pair's WBNB reserve from the block immediately before the exploit through the exploit block. The exploiter later agreed to return 80%; recovery is separate from exploit-time gross loss.
The $8.9 million value is a rounded reported incident-time valuation; the exact onchain WBNB reserve decrease is structured separately.
Later recovery is intentionally separate from the exploit-time gross loss.
